local_state_rules: Pathogen load activates innate response, cytokines recruit adaptive cells, and excessive cytokines raise inflammation risk.
Anti-inflammatory treatment should reduce cytokine burden but may slow pathogen clearance depending on timing.
Cell counts, signal arrows, pathogen load, inflammation score, and explanation must share one cascade state.
difficulty_profile: time stepping, cell populations, cytokine arrows, risk gauges, and event log must stay synchronized
later turns add stimulus strength, cytokine storm threshold, treatment/recovery comparison, and prediction challenge
visual object must resemble an immune response scene with cells and signals, not only line charts
task_world.visual_object_requirement: Render a tissue cross-section or immune-response board with macrophages, T cells, cytokine signals, pathogen load, inflammation gauge, and intervention controls.

validation_scenarios.name: cascade time-step sync
validation_scenarios.public_requirement_ref: T1 asks: Explain cytokine cascades in an immune response, then build an interactive tissue-response lab where I can step time forward and watch pathogen load, macrophages, T cells, cytokine signals, and inflammation risk change together.
validation_scenarios.oracle: The UI satisfies turn 1 of Immune Response Cytokine Cascade Lab: time stepping updates pathogen, cells, cytokines, inflammation risk, and event log together. Pass requires executed UI evidence for the stated mechanism; component presence, source-code intent, or a single easy happy path is insufficient. Actor reference: verify the action/evidence checklist through visible UI operations; do not finish success from component presence, source intent, or an unrelated easier interaction.

evidence_requirements.expect: tissue board / counts / signal arrows
time stepping updates pathogen, cells, cytokines, inflammation risk, and event log together

evidence_requirements.surface: visible controls / primary visual / derived readouts
evidence_requirements.expect: At least two independent surfaces change consistently from the same canonical state; a static diagram plus unrelated readout is insufficient.
evidence_requirements.action: Use the central state-changing control for this turn, record baseline state, change it through visible UI, and compare at least two dependent surfaces. Do not use source code alone as evidence.
evidence_requirements.evidence: Quote the before/after control value and two dependent visible outputs. If only a label changes while dependent surfaces do not, report failure.

evidence_requirements.expect: The UI must update according to the domain rule or explicitly explain why the state is impossible; stale values, impossible success states, or generic success text count as failure.
evidence_requirements.action: Exercise one high/low, valid/invalid, legal/blocked, narrow/wide, or correct/wrong contrast implied by the public request. Prefer a contrast with a predicted qualitative outcome.
evidence_requirements.evidence: Record the contrast, expected domain outcome, and observed UI outcome. Do not replace a failed public contrast with an easier passing example.

evidence_requirements.expect: All linked surfaces must agree on the same selected entity, time, scenario, threshold, object id, or parameter value; stale or detached surfaces are failure.
evidence_requirements.action: Change the primary selection, parameter, or scenario and inspect every linked surface named by the task.
evidence_requirements.evidence: Record the selected state and at least three linked surfaces when present. Name any surface that remains stale, out of sync, or unreachable.

validation_scenarios.fairness_risk: Evaluate only the represented current controls and task-local rules; do not require external real-world fidelity beyond the public request. Do not let actor/evaluator substitute an easier example after a public or UI-advertised boundary case fails; count stale linked views, dummy controls, and impossible success states as real failures. If actor tooling cannot operate a visible drag/slider directly, try an actor-supported visible alternative on the same control; if the primary mechanism remains unreachable, record that as evidence instead of substituting a different feature.
